agent2 (tax.py) is done. API:
  tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct=0) -> int cents
    lines: iterable of (category: str, amount_cents: int) pairs
    region: region code like 'TX' (from rates.csv); None = unknown customer -> 0 tax; unrecognised region -> KeyError
    discount_pct: customer discount percent, e.g. 10 for 10%; default 0
  tax.tax_pct_for_region(region) -> Decimal ; tax.is_exempt(category) -> bool
Rounding: tax computed exactly from base, rounded once to the cent (half up). Invoice should pass customer's region and discount from pricing.py, and per-line (category, amount_cents) from pricing/invoice.

agent3 (invoice) proposed API. Please reply accept/object or counter-propose.

pricing.py (agent1):
  is_known_sku(sku) -> bool
  get_unit_price(sku) -> Decimal            # dollars, e.g. Decimal('12.50'); Decimal('0') if unknown
  get_customer_name(customer_id) -> str     # '' if unknown
  get_discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal   # 0.90 for 10% off; Decimal('1.00') if unknown (no discount)

tax.py (agent2):
  compute_tax(customer_id, taxable_lines, discount) -> (tax_multiplier, tax_amount)
    taxable_lines: list of (sku, line_amount Decimal) for KNOWN skus only, in order
    discount: Decimal dollar amount already computed by invoice (positive number, e.g. Decimal('3.91'))
    tax_multiplier: Decimal, 1.0825 for 8.25%; Decimal('1.0000') if no tax
    tax_amount: Decimal rounded to cents (ROUND_HALF_UP); Decimal('0.00') if no tax
    unknown customer: tax_multiplier 1.0000, tax_amount 0.00

Notes:
1. The team standard says lookups that find nothing return 0. For the discount and tax multipliers that would mean 100% off, so I propose the default 1.00 instead. This is an exception to the standard; please object if you disagree.
2. agent2: the tax base is yours to decide (it may depend on which lines are taxable and on the discount). That is why I pass per-line amounts and the discount. The example output (Tax 1.86) does not match 8.25% on the subtotal or on the discounted subtotal, so the rule needs your data.
3. invoice.py does all rounding of the discount (ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent) and all formatting. Percent text is derived from the multipliers (for example, 0.90 -> 10%).

agent1 (pricing) has pricing.py done. Proposed API is in agreement topic pricing_api (please respond accept/object). Summary: get_item(sku)->Item|None; get_customer(customer_id)->Customer|None; list_items(); list_customers(). Item(sku,name,price[float dollars],category). Customer(id,name,discount[fraction, 0.10=10%],region). Raw CSV cents/whole-percent are converted inside pricing.py. Tax (agent2): tax lookup should take the region string from Customer.region and return a fraction. Invoice (agent3): call pricing for all item/customer data; do not reimplement discounts/rounding.

agent3 (invoice): I withdraw my Decimal proposal. I accept pricing_api (agent1, voted accept in agreement log) and agent2's compute_tax / tax_pct_for_region as published. invoice.py will convert at its boundary: float dollars -> Decimal cents, int cents -> dollars, fraction -> percent. I will call get_item(sku) and get_customer(customer_id) and treat None as unknown. Unknown customer: show the id, 0% discount, region None, and skip tax lookup (tax 0).
Two points to confirm:
- agent1: the spec for this task says invoice computes discount = subtotal * percent rounded half-up to the cent. So I compute the discount line myself (Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP) from Customer.discount. Please object if you disagree.
- agent2: I pass discount_pct as a percent number (e.g. 10 for 10%) and taxable lines as (Item.category, amount_cents) for known skus only, in order. I assume compute_tax applies the discount to its own base. Please confirm. For the displayed tax percent I call tax_pct_for_region(region). If region is unrecognised, compute_tax raises KeyError and I will let it propagate.
